title: Map Development using Astra
author: Ok-Librarian-1265
selftext:
Hey everyone! I'm currently vibe coding a small game for fun and need some workflow advice.

I’m using a purchased asset pack alongside Astra, but whenever I try generating maps/scenes, it just looks like random assets dumped onto a screen.

I'm not sure what is the best method when doing this, so hoping someone here might have some insight.

* Is it better to feed the model a visual reference/rough layout sketch first?
* Does cranking up to a higher-effort reasoning model work better?

Any help would be great. Thanks!

comments.author: UnderStrangeStars
comments.body:
I've not used Astra, and I don't do AI development -- but this is what I would try.

  
Find references. Make a few small examples yourself with your reference to provide a template. 

Even for my own purposes I build massive mood boards of things to do and patterns to avoid. I create a few studies / examples... like how to handle the edges of a forest, how to cluster within a forest. Layering I like vs layering I don't like. Rock sizes.. scales... etc

Spend some time, at least 20 hours manually doing this process. Then hand it to Astra. 20 hours sounds like a lot, but designing a may with lots of terrain is usually 100s of hours.

comments.author: ShinyangAU
comments.body:
the trick with effectively using AI is actually two parts. 

You as the designer have to lead the creativity part. Just do very rough outlines of how you want the map to look, pathways, elevation, deadlines etc. AI can then use that 'rough template' and essentially do a v1.0 polish in very high thinking mode. Then you review it, prompt it to fine tune further in medium or high mode.

There's still a bit of ground work on our end, but think of the AI as an assistant to bounce off. An assistant can't generally start from the ground without being lead the path first? if that makes any sense.

comments.author: BanjoThunderbird
comments.body: You're being lazy and not describing what you want in enough detail. Tell it where to put everything exactly according to your vision. If you don't actually know where you want things, then start from the ground up and place one thing at a time. Then repeatedly tweak until it's perfectly aligned with what you wanted. You can use a drawing to communicate more detail or plan it out for yourself, but ultimately you're just not providing enough instruction. The AI model or reasoning level is not relevant.

comments.author: Jolly_Roger-99
comments.body: For the ground use layers. Check youtube on a pbr Tutorial
